results.title: Generator rank
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a topological group $G$, the generator rank $d(G)$ is the least natural number $k$ such that some finite subset of $G$ with $k$ elements generates a dense subgroup of $G$, that is, a subgroup whose closure is all of $G$. If no finite subset of $G$ generates a dense subgroup, then $d(G)$ is defined to be $0$. For a finite discrete group this is the ordinary minimal number of generators.

results.title: Trivial representation on $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $p$ and a topological group $G$, this is $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$, with its discrete topology, regarded as a continuous representation of $G$ over $\mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ on which every element of $G$ acts as the identity.

results.title: Relation rank
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a prime $p$ and a topological group $G$, the relation rank $r(G)$ is the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_p = \mathbb{Z}/p\mathbb{Z}$ of the continuous cohomology group $H^2(G, \mathbb{F}_p)$, where $G$ acts trivially on $\mathbb{F}_p$. If this space is infinite-dimensional, then $r(G)$ is defined to be $0$.

results.title: Golod–Shafarevich inequality
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $p$ be a prime and let $Q$ be a nontrivial finite $p$-group, viewed as a topological group with the discrete topology. Then the generator rank $d(Q)$ and the relation rank $r(Q)$, the dimension over $\mathbb{F}_p$ of the continuous cohomology group $H^2(Q, \mathbb{F}_p)$ with trivial coefficients, satisfy $d(Q)^2 < 4\, r(Q)$.

results.title: Dickson's classification, tame case

results.title: Norm of a cusp form

results.title: Fibonacci factorial
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: For a natural number $n$, the Fibonacci factorial $F_n!$ is the rational number $F_n! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_n$, the product of the first $n$ Fibonacci numbers (where $F_1 = F_2 = 1$ and $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$); in particular $F_0! = 1$, the empty product.

results.title: Fibonacci factorials are positive

results.title: Fibonacci factorials are nonzero

results.title: Fibonacci factorial at one

results.title: Generalized FiboCatalan numbers
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $F_m! = F_1 F_2 \cdots F_m$ denote the Fibonacci factorial of the Fibonacci numbers $F_1 = F_2 = 1$, $F_{k+2} = F_{k+1} + F_k$ (so $F_0! = 1$), and let $J_{r,F} = F_{2r+1}! / F_r!$ be the Fibonacci Jordan quotient. results.title: Half-tape view of a stack tape

results.summary: A stack tape $s$ over an alphabet $\Gamma$ is a finite list of cells, each a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank cell, that does not end in a blank cell. Its half-tape view is the half-tape of cells (a sequence of cells taken up to trailing blanks, the blank cell being the default) whose cells are those of $s$ in order, followed by blank cells.

results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The half-tape view of the empty stack tape over $\Gamma$ is the half-tape all of whose cells are blank.

results.title: Pushing a cell onto a stack tape
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every cell $c$ (a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank cell) and every stack tape $s$ over $\Gamma$, the half-tape view of the stack tape obtained by pushing $c$ onto $s$ is the half-tape view of $s$ with $c$ pushed onto its front.

results.title: Tail of the half-tape view of a stack tape
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every stack tape $s$ over $\Gamma$ (a list of cells, each a symbol of $\Gamma$ or the blank cell, not ending in a blank cell), the tail of the half-tape view of $s$ is the half-tape view of the tail of $s$: dropping the first cell of $s$ drops the first cell of its half-tape.

results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet with blank symbol $b$. A tape cell over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ is either blank or holds a symbol $x \ne b$ of $\Gamma_0$. Its cell symbol is $b$ for the blank cell and $x$ for the cell holding $x$. This map from cells to $\Gamma_0$ sends the blank cell to the blank symbol, so it is a pointed map.

results.title: Value of the cell-symbol map
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every cell $o$ over the non-blank symbols of an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$, the cell symbol of $o$ is $b$ when $o$ is the blank cell and is $x$ when $o$ holds the non-blank symbol $x$.

results.title: The cell-symbol map is injective
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Distinct cells over the non-blank symbols of an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ have distinct cell symbols in $\Gamma_0$.

results.title: Half-tape of a stack tape of non-blank symbols
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet with blank symbol $b$ and $N = \Gamma_0 \setminus \{b\}$ its non-blank symbols. A stack tape $s$ over $N$, a finite list of cells each blank or holding a symbol of $N$ and not ending in a blank cell, is read as the TM0 half-tape over $\Gamma_0$ whose $i$-th symbol is that of the $i$-th cell of $s$: $b$ for a blank cell, $x$ for a cell holding $x$, and $b$ past the end of $s$.

results.title: The empty stack tape reads as the blank half-tape
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$, the empty stack tape over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ reads as the half-tape of the empty list, all of whose symbols are $b$.

results.title: Pushing a cell onto a stack tape of non-blank symbols
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet with blank symbol $b$ and $N = \Gamma_0 \setminus \{b\}$. For every cell $o$ and every stack tape $s$ over $N$, the half-tape read from the stack tape obtained by pushing $o$ onto $s$ is the half-tape read from $s$ with the symbol of $o$ pushed onto its front.

results.title: First symbol of a half-tape read from non-blank cells
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet with blank symbol $b$. For every stack tape $s$ of cells over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ (a finite list of cells, blank beyond its end), the first symbol of the half-tape over $\Gamma_0$ read from $s$ is the cell symbol of the first cell of $s$; when $s$ is empty this is $b$.

results.title: Dropping the first cell of a stack tape of non-blank symbols
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$ and every stack tape $s$ over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$, dropping the first symbol of the half-tape read from $s$ gives the half-tape read from $s$ with its first cell removed (the empty stack tape staying empty).

results.title: A word of non-blank symbols reads as itself
results.caption: Theorem

results.title: Distinct stack tapes of non-blank symbols read as distinct half-tapes
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$, two stack tapes over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ that read as the same half-tape over $\Gamma_0$ are equal.

results.title: Head symbol of a tape read from non-blank cells
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: For every two-way tape $t$ of cells over the non-blank symbols of an alphabet $\Gamma_0$, the symbol under the head of the tape over $\Gamma_0$ read from $t$ is the cell symbol of the cell under the head of $t$.

results.summary: Let $\Gamma_0$ be an alphabet whose default symbol is the blank, and for a two-way tape $t$ whose cells are blank or hold non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$, let $\tau(t)$ be the Post–Turing reading of $t$, a Post–Turing machine tape over $\Gamma_0$. results.title: The Post–Turing reading of an input tape

results.summary: For an alphabet $\Gamma_0$ with blank symbol $b$, two tapes over the non-blank symbols of $\Gamma_0$ that read, cell by cell, as the same TM0 tape over $\Gamma_0$ are equal.

results.title: Haplotype window around the core
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The window of radius `d` of haplotype `i`: its alleles at the `d` sites closest to the core, in the direction indexed by `ℕ`.

results.title: Equality of haplotype windows
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Two haplotypes have the same window of radius `d` exactly when they agree at every site `k < d`.

results.title: Concordant haplotype pairs at a given radius
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of ordered pairs of distinct haplotypes of `C` whose windows of radius `d` agree.

results.title: Extended haplotype homozygosity (EHH)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Extended haplotype homozygosity at radius `d` of the haplotype set `C`: the probability that two distinct haplotypes drawn from `C` without replacement agree at all `d` sites nearest the core (Sabeti et al. 2002). For `#C ≤ 1` the denominator vanishes and the junk value `0` is returned; every statement below that needs the probabilistic reading assumes `2 ≤ #C`.

results.title: EHH is zero for a set of at most one haplotype
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: Outside the domain `2 ≤ #C` the definition returns the junk value `0`.

results.title: EHH at radius zero equals one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: At radius `0` every pair of haplotypes agrees, so `EHH(0) = 1`.

results.title: EHH is nonincreasing in the radius
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: EHH is nonincreasing in the radius: widening the window can only break ties.

results.title: EHH as homozygosity of window-type counts
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: EHH as the sampling-without-replacement homozygosity of the partition of `C` into window types: `EHH(d) = ∑_t c_t (c_t - 1) / (#C (#C - 1))`, where `c_t` is the number of haplotypes of `C` with window `t`. This is the form in which EHH is usually defined.

results.title: Concordant haplotype pairs sharing a core allele
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The number of ordered pairs of distinct haplotypes of `C` whose core alleles (under `core`) agree and whose windows of radius `d` agree. The extended haplotype includes the core, so pairs carrying different core alleles are never concordant, even when their outward windows match.

results.title: Extended haplotype homozygosity with core-allele labels
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Extended haplotype homozygosity with core-allele labels: the probability that two distinct haplotypes drawn from `C` without replacement share both their core allele and their window of radius `d`. For a set `C` of carriers of a single core allele this is the same count as `ehh`; for a pooled set `D` carrying several core alleles it excludes the cross-core pairs that plain `ehh` would wrongly count as concordant.

results.title: Relative extended haplotype homozygosity (REHH)
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: Relative extended haplotype homozygosity: the core-labelled EHH of the core-allele carriers `C` divided by the core-labelled EHH of the pooled set `D` of haplotypes carrying the other core alleles. The denominator counts only pairs sharing a core allele, so cross-core pairs never inflate it. This is the statistic of the long-range haplotype test (Sabeti et al. 2002). It is a junk value `0` when the denominator…

results.title: Criterion for relative EHH to exceed one
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: With a positive reference EHH, the relative EHH exceeds `1` exactly when the core allele's haplotypes are the more homozygous ones.

results.title: Probability of no recombination on a pair's genealogy
results.caption: Definition
results.summary: The probability that no recombination falls on the genealogy of a pair of lineages within genetic distance `d` of the core, given that the pair coalesces at time `t` (time in units of `2N` generations, `ρ = 4Nr` the scaled recombination rate per site): the two lineages carry recombination events at total rate `ρ * d` until they coalesce.

results.title: No-recombination probability decays with distance
results.caption: Theorem
results.summary: The no-recombination probability decays in the distance from the core.

results.title: Mean no-recombination probability under the neutral coalescent
results.caption: Theorem
